auditor_value: (a) relative to the car: uniform deceleration 5 m/s² in +î, momentary rest at t = 2 s and x_rel = 10 m, then acceleration 5 m/s² in −î; (b) back at the start at t = 4 s

findings.quote: Taking the return time as when the object's own velocity returns to 10 m/s (never happens) instead of solving x_rel = 0 gives no finite answer.
findings.note: Not a recognisable student error and internally muddled: in the ground frame the object's velocity is 10 m/s throughout (so 'never happens' is false), and in the car frame the relative velocity goes from +10 to −10 m/s and does not return to +10. A student's real slip here is to take the moment of momentary rest (t = 2 s) as the return time.
findings.fix: Taking the instant when the object is momentarily at rest relative to the car (t = 2 s) as the return time; at that instant it is 10 m ahead of its starting point and only reaches the start again at t = 4 s.

question_defect: The served question text prints parts (a) and (b) twice (once inline, once as separate lines).
notes: Ground-frame object velocity stays 10 m/s because the car is at rest at t = 0; x_rel = 10t − 2.5t² = 0 at t = 4 s, matching the solution.
